_comment: Reference universe for the Competitive Intelligence Engine (scripts/profitdecoded/collect-competitors.js). Handles are resolved through the API (forHandle); a handle that does not resolve is reported, never guessed. Chosen from the Phase 1 public-page review (docs/profitdecoded/PHASE-1-STRATEGY.md, 2026-10-08): channels whose recent uploads sit inside 'the business behind everyday life', weighted toward small channels with views well above their subscriber count. Large channels are included only as category benchmarks when their topics overlap ours. The phase1Observation text is what a person read on public pages on 2026-10-08; it is context for humans, the collector never reads it as data. Small and new channels are found by keyword discovery (queries), not listed here.

referenceChannels.name: Micro
referenceChannels.why: faceless 3D-rendered consumer/economy documentaries; strongest small-channel ratio in our niche
referenceChannels.phase1Observation: 208K subscribers, 42 videos; Costco local-economy video 3.0M, shipbuilding 3.1M

referenceChannels.name: Neu
referenceChannels.why: faceless 8-10 min 'economics of' explainers; one video at about 16x its subscriber count
referenceChannels.phase1Observation: 37.5K subscribers, 47 videos; 'The Economics of Owning A Ship' 619K

referenceChannels.name: Established Context
referenceChannels.why: US consumer-economy explainers; one breakout carried the channel
referenceChannels.phase1Observation: 66.7K subscribers; Costco business-model video 1.58M; last upload about 4 months before observation

referenceChannels.name: Tony Talks Business
referenceChannels.why: daily 'how X makes money' uploads; shows what the template earns at volume

referenceChannels.name: Hidden Economics
referenceChannels.why: new channel with an extreme early ratio; cause unknown, watch before drawing conclusions

referenceChannels.name: Modern MBA
referenceChannels.why: long-form business-model documentaries on everyday businesses (buffets, pizzerias, car rental, theaters)

referenceChannels.name: Wendover Productions
referenceChannels.why: covers many of our obvious topics (fast food prices, car dealers, IKEA)

referenceChannels.name: The Fat Files
referenceChannels.why: US consumer-brand stories at about 1-2.8M per video; NOT faceless (host-led), so a demand ceiling, not a format to copy
referenceChannels.phase1Observation: 881K subscribers, 55 videos; Planet Fitness 1.9M, mattress stores 1.96M

referenceChannels.name: Company Man
referenceChannels.why: US company decline/success stories; long-running series format

referenceChannels.name: Logically Answered
referenceChannels.why: company failure stories (Dollar Shave Club 1.4M); more tech/news-driven than us

referenceChannels.name: Mr. Finance
referenceChannels.why: near-daily 'The Economics of Owning a ___' uploads; tracks how saturated that template is

removedOn2026-10-08.reason: large or off-niche channels whose baselines would hide outliers in our topics
removedOn2026-10-08.note: WSJ 'The Economics Of', Business Insider 'So Expensive' and CNBC still prove demand for many topics; they appear in coverage observations and keyword discovery, but their channel baselines are dominated by news uploads
